tools.name: Aareon
tools.positioning: The European ERP of social and institutional housing — where the tenant file, the rent and the works order live together.
tools.description: Aareon provides enterprise property management software for social landlords, institutional owners and large managers across Europe, with a French organisation serving bailleurs sociaux: tenant and lease management, rent and charge accounting, allocation processes, maintenance and tenant self-service portals.
tools.real_estate_use: French social housing operates under rules no commercial system covers: regulated rents, the allocation commission, the surface and resource ceilings, the supplément de loyer. Aareon's French deployments encode those processes, which is why the sector runs on specialised ERPs rather than on general property management platforms.
features: Tenant, lease and allocation management for regulated housing
Rent and charge accounting with regulatory rules
Maintenance and works order management
Tenant self-service portal and digital services
Asset and patrimony management
Regulatory and management reporting

use_cases.job: Run regulated allocation and rent processes for a social housing portfolio
Hold asset, lease and works data for a large institutional patrimony in one ERP

tools.name: Aptexx
tools.positioning: A mobile-first resident experience platform bundling rent payments, messaging and maintenance tracking for property managers.
tools.description: Aptexx is a resident experience platform for rental property managers, combining online rent payment processing (cards, mobile wallets, ACH, bank transfer, cash), resident messaging and emergency alerts, survey collection, and maintenance and package tracking behind a single admin dashboard.
tools.real_estate_use: A property manager collects rent online through Aptexx instead of chasing checks, and uses the same portal to send building-wide alerts, run resident satisfaction surveys, and track maintenance requests. Bilingual residents get the app's built-in English-Spanish translation rather than a manager translating messages by hand.
features: Online rent payment processing (cards, ACH, mobile wallets, cash)
Resident messaging and emergency alerts
Maintenance request tracking
Package tracking
Admin dashboard with portfolio reporting
Built-in English-Spanish translation

use_cases.job: Collect rent online and reconcile payments from a single dashboard
Pay rent, request maintenance and receive building alerts from a phone

tools.name: Building Engines
tools.positioning: Prism, the building operations platform property teams at JLL, CBRE and Hines use to run work orders and tenant compliance.
tools.description: Building Engines, a JLL company, publishes Prism, a building operations platform for commercial real estate covering work orders, bid management, preventive maintenance, tenant insurance compliance, inspections and incident tracking, alongside a tenant-facing module for resource reservations and visitor access.
tools.real_estate_use: A building engineer dispatches and closes out work orders through Prism instead of a spreadsheet, and the same platform tracks whether every tenant's certificate of insurance is current before a compliance deadline. On the tenant side, an occupant books a shared conference room or registers a visitor through Prism's tenant experience module rather than emailing the front desk.
features: Work order and bid management
Preventive maintenance scheduling
Tenant insurance compliance tracking
Inspections and incident tracking
Tenant resource reservations and visitor access
Mobile app

use_cases.job: Dispatch and close out work orders and track preventive maintenance across a portfolio
Track tenant certificate-of-insurance compliance ahead of deadlines

tools.name: ButterflyMX
tools.positioning: Cloud-based property access: video intercoms, keypads and smart locks a resident answers from their phone and a manager administers from a browser.
tools.description: ButterflyMX sells a connected access-control system for buildings, combining door hardware with a resident smartphone app and a management console. The product line covers video intercoms, a QR-code intercom, keypads, smart locks, elevator controls, vehicle access control, security cameras, package rooms and a front-desk station. Residents see and speak to whoever is at the door or gate, open it remotely and issue temporary access PINs; managers review entry logs, grant or revoke access and connect the system to other cloud tools. The company states the installation requires only three connections — internet, power and an electronic or magnetic lock — which removes the in-unit hardware and building wiring a traditional intercom needs.
tools.real_estate_use: A property manager running a multifamily building without a doorman needs deliveries, contractors and guests to get in without anyone driving to the site with a key. They install ButterflyMX at the entrance, and from then on a courier calls the unit, the resident answers on their phone wherever they are, and the door opens; the manager issues a dated PIN to the cleaning company and revokes it when the contract ends. When a dispute arises over who entered and when, the entry log settles it. Leasing teams also use the self-guided tour feature so a prospect can visit a vacant unit without an agent present.
features: Video intercom answered from a resident smartphone app
Remote door and gate release, with temporary access PINs
Building entry logs and per-user access administration
Keypads, smart locks and elevator controls on the same system
Package room and front-desk station modules
Self-guided tour access for prospective renters

use_cases.job: Let couriers and contractors into a staffless building and keep a reviewable log of every entry
See and admit a visitor at the building entrance from anywhere, without being home
Cut intercom wiring and in-unit hardware out of a new building's access-control budget

tools.name: Condo Control
tools.positioning: Condo and HOA management software organised around the building's daily life: communication, amenities, security desk and maintenance, with accounting alongside.
tools.description: Condo Control is software for condominium and homeowner association management, sold to management companies, self-managed communities and security companies. Its modules cover communication (announcements, discussion forum, association websites, virtual meetings and an AI manager assistant), financial work (accounting, billing and collections, portfolio accounting, reports and budgeting, online payments, vendor management), maintenance (requests, architectural change, preventive maintenance, community assets), record keeping (resident database, file library, violation tracking, proxy and fractional voting, electronic consent), security (authorised entry, incident reports, key tracking, security logs and patrol, package management) and the resident side (guest passes, event calendar, amenity booking, package tracking, visitor parking). The vendor also sells managed accounting and moderated meeting services alongside the software.
tools.real_estate_use: A condominium tower runs on things a rental building never has to think about: a front desk logging visitors, a party room booked three weeks ahead, a package wall that overflows every December, a proxy count that has to hold up at the annual general meeting. Condo Control is the product that treats those as first-class, which is why concierge and security staff use it as much as the property manager. A manager reaches for it when the building's problem is coordination rather than accounting, and when the board wants residents to self-serve on bookings, documents and payments instead of calling the office. Its pricing is quoted per unit band with distinct plans for self-managed communities and for management companies.
features: Amenity booking, guest passes and visitor parking
Package tracking and package room management
Front desk security logs, patrol, incident reports and key tracking
Violation tracking and rule enforcement
Proxy and fractional voting with electronic consent
Maintenance requests, preventive maintenance and architectural change requests

use_cases.job: Run an AGM with a proxy count that holds up, without paper
Book the party room and see whether a package has arrived without calling the desk
Track a maintenance request from a resident report to a vendor visit

tools.name: CredHub
tools.positioning: Reports resident rent payments to the major credit bureaus every month, on-time and late alike.
tools.description: CredHub is a rent payment credit reporting service for property managers and landlords. It reports both on-time and missed rent payments to Equifax, Experian, TransUnion and Innovis each month, integrates with property management systems, and bundles identity protection for residents through a partnership with Allstate.
tools.real_estate_use: A property manager with at least 50 units offers CredHub as a resident benefit so on-time rent starts building credit automatically, without either party filing anything each month. The manager also gets a delinquency lever: because late payments are reported too, residents have a direct credit incentive to pay on time, which CredHub's own figures link to roughly half the rent delinquency of comparable properties.
features: Monthly rent payment reporting to four credit bureaus
Reports both on-time and late/missed payments
Property management system integrations
Dedicated U.S.-based account management
Bundled resident identity protection (Allstate)

use_cases.job: Offer rent-reporting as a resident benefit that also discourages late payment
Build credit history automatically by paying rent on time

tools.name: Equiem
tools.positioning: Tenant experience with an editorial team behind it — the content is the product, not just the app shell.
tools.description: Equiem provides a tenant app and portal for office and mixed-use buildings covering communications, bookings, access, retail offers and events, differentiated by managed content services that produce building communications on the landlord's behalf.
tools.real_estate_use: Most tenant apps fail from emptiness: nobody at the landlord has time to post anything, so occupants stop opening it. Equiem sells the editorial capacity alongside the platform, which is why it is chosen by landlords who want engagement without hiring a community manager per building.
features: Tenant app and web portal for a building or campus
Managed content and communications services
Amenity, room and event booking
Retail and service offers with local vendors
Access control integration and mobile credentials
Engagement and utilisation analytics

use_cases.job: Keep a tenant app genuinely used without hiring a community manager per building
Communicate building notices and events to occupants directly

tools.name: essensys
tools.positioning: The infrastructure layer under flex space — network, access and billing for buildings running many operators.
tools.description: essensys provides software and on-site technology for flexible workspace: operations and billing platform, plus network infrastructure that segments and provisions connectivity per tenant, and access control across multi-tenant buildings.
tools.real_estate_use: A landlord converting floors to flex has a problem no coworking app solves: every occupier needs its own secure network segment, provisioned in hours rather than weeks, and metered. essensys sits at that layer, which is why it is bought by landlords and large operators rather than by single spaces.
features: Per-tenant network provisioning and segmentation
Automated billing for space, services and consumption
Access control across multi-tenant buildings
Operations platform for flexible workspace portfolios
Real-time service usage metering
Landlord-grade reporting across operators

use_cases.job: Turn floors into flex space with secure per-occupier networks provisioned in hours
Meter and bill services consumed by multiple operators in one building

tools.name: Esusu
tools.positioning: A rent-reporting and financial wellness platform that turns on-time rent into credit history for residents.
tools.description: Esusu is a fintech platform for real estate operators built around rent reporting: it reports payments to Experian, Equifax and TransUnion so residents build credit, and layers on flexible payment options, income and identity fraud verification, financial coaching and portfolio analytics for property owners.
tools.real_estate_use: A multifamily operator rolls out Esusu across a portfolio so residents' on-time rent is reported to the three bureaus without extra paperwork, while the operator's screening team uses the same platform's identity and income verification to catch fraudulent applications before move-in. During renewal season, the operator's analytics dashboard shows which properties are seeing the credit-building benefit move renewal rates.
features: Rent reporting to three major credit bureaus
Identity, income and SSN fraud verification
Flexible rent payment options (Affirm, split pay)
Financial coaching and marketplace access
Portfolio analytics dashboard

use_cases.job: Report resident rent payments to credit bureaus across a portfolio
Build credit history and access flexible rent payment options

tools.name: FRONTSTEPS
tools.positioning: A set of connected HOA products covering back-office accounting, resident engagement, payments and community access control under one ecosystem.
tools.description: FRONTSTEPS sells a family of products for homeowner association operations rather than a single application. Caliber handles community budgets and daily financial tasks with automated workflows, reporting and document organisation. Community provides mobile applications for managers, boards and residents with a resident engagement programme. Payments lets homeowners pay assessments online through a PCI DSS compliant processor. Manager is the web-based back office for community association managers working in the field. A safety and security line covers visitor access control and community monitoring inside the same application.
tools.real_estate_use: A community association manager's day splits between a desk and a gate: assessments to post, a board packet to prepare, and then a visitor list, an amenity, a patrol log. FRONTSTEPS is assembled for firms that want those two halves under one vendor, with Caliber as the accounting spine and the resident and access products hanging off it. It suits a management company whose communities are gated or amenity-heavy, where access control is not an add-on but part of what the board is paying for. Because the offer is a set of products rather than one, the practical question at purchase is which pieces a firm actually takes.
features: Caliber community accounting with automated financial workflows and reporting
Resident and board mobile applications with an engagement programme
Online assessment payments through a PCI DSS compliant processor
Web-based manager back office usable in the field
Visitor access control and community security monitoring
Document organisation and customisable financial rules

use_cases.job: Run association accounting and gate access from the same vendor
Pay an assessment online instead of mailing a cheque

tools.name: HqO
tools.positioning: The landlord's app for the people who work in the building — and the measurement of whether they come in.
tools.description: HqO is a workplace experience platform for office landlords and occupiers: a tenant-facing app for access, amenities, bookings, events and communications, plus an analytics layer measuring how a building is actually used.
tools.real_estate_use: Since hybrid work, an office landlord's asset value depends on whether tenants renew, and renewal depends on whether employees turn up. HqO gives the landlord a direct channel to occupants rather than only to the tenant's facilities contact, and produces the utilisation data used in renewal conversations and in amenity investment decisions.
features: Tenant experience app with building access and mobile credentials
Amenity, room and service booking
Building communications, events and community features
Workplace utilisation analytics and benchmarking
Tenant satisfaction measurement
Integrations with access control and building systems

use_cases.job: Measure building utilisation to support a renewal or amenity investment case
Access the building, book a room and see what is on today from one app

tools.name: PayHOA
tools.positioning: Online HOA management for self-managed associations, sold at a published price per community with a free trial and no sales call.
tools.description: PayHOA is a US web application for managing a homeowners association online. Its financial side covers general ledger accounting, budgets and board reports, bank integrations that remove manual transaction entry, payables and vendor approvals, and an optional bookkeeping service. Its communication side covers mass text, email and phone messaging, one-click USPS mailings through a mailroom feature, private message boards and a website builder. Its management side covers CC&R violation tracking, request forms, document storage, online voting and surveys, owner portals and resale documents. The vendor states it is used by more than 6,000 communities.
tools.real_estate_use: Most American associations have no management company at all: a volunteer treasurer collects dues, keeps the books in a spreadsheet and mails paper notices. PayHOA is built for that person. It is the rare product in this category that publishes its price per community size and opens with a free trial rather than a demo, which is what makes it reachable for a board with no budget line for software. The mailroom feature matters more than it sounds, because an association is often legally obliged to send notices by post and doing that by hand is the treasurer's worst evening of the year. Management companies use it too, but its centre of gravity is the self-managed board.
features: General ledger accounting with budgets and board reports
Bank integrations removing manual transaction entry
Payables and vendor approval workflow
Mass communication by text, email and phone
Mailroom for one-click USPS postal mailings
CC&R violation tracking and resident request forms

use_cases.job: Collect dues online and produce board financials without a management company
Send a legally required notice by post without handling envelopes

tools.name: SmartRent
tools.positioning: Smart apartment hardware and software sold to the operator, not to the resident.
tools.description: SmartRent provides smart home hardware and a management platform for rental housing: smart locks, thermostats, leak sensors, self-guided tour access, community access control and parking, managed centrally by the operator across a portfolio.
tools.real_estate_use: Three operational cases drive the purchase. Self-guided tours let a prospect visit a vacant unit without staff. Smart locks remove the key handover and the lock change at turnover. Leak sensors catch water damage — the largest avoidable insurance claim in multifamily — before it reaches the unit below.
features: Smart locks with credential management at turnover
Self-guided tour access for prospective residents
Thermostat control on vacant units
Leak detection and water shut-off alerting
Community access control and parking management
Portfolio-wide device management and alerts

use_cases.job: Offer self-guided tours of vacant units without on-site staff
Reduce water damage claims and turnover costs across a portfolio

tools.name: SpinalCom
tools.positioning: A building operating system — the layer that makes twenty proprietary building systems queryable as one digital twin.
tools.description: SpinalCom publishes a building operating system that aggregates data from heterogeneous building systems — HVAC, lighting, access, metering, BIM models — into a semantic digital twin, exposed through APIs so applications can be built on top rather than integrated one by one.
tools.real_estate_use: A smart building project usually stalls on the same wall: every subsystem speaks a different protocol and belongs to a different contractor. Placing an operating system between the equipment and the applications means the tenant app, the energy dashboard and the maintenance tool all read the same model of the building, and replacing a supplier does not break everything above it.
features: Aggregation of heterogeneous building systems and protocols
Semantic digital twin linked to the BIM model
Open APIs for third-party applications
Real-time supervision and equipment monitoring
Data historisation for energy and operations analytics
Vendor-independent architecture

use_cases.job: Read every building subsystem through one model instead of twenty interfaces
Build tenant and energy applications on a twin that outlives a supplier change

tools.name: Ubigreen
tools.positioning: Energy and space usage measured together — because an empty floor that is still heated is both problems at once.
tools.description: Ubigreen provides French building operators with energy performance monitoring, regulatory declaration support, and workplace occupancy measurement, combining consumption data with presence and space-use data in one platform.
tools.real_estate_use: Since hybrid work, the two questions arrived together: how much energy does this building use, and how much of it is actually occupied. Measuring both allows the decision that follows — consolidating occupancy onto fewer floors and shutting down the rest, which moves consumption far more than any equipment upgrade.
features: Energy consumption monitoring across multi-site portfolios
Décret tertiaire and OPERAT declaration support
Workplace occupancy and space utilisation measurement
Comfort and indoor environment monitoring
Alerting on consumption drift and equipment faults
Reporting for occupants and management

use_cases.job: Consolidate occupancy onto fewer floors and shut down the energy on the rest
Declare regulated consumption and track the effect of measures taken

tools.name: VTS
tools.positioning: The leasing pipeline for office landlords — every tour, proposal and lease in one view, plus a demand index nobody else has.
tools.description: VTS is a leasing and asset management platform for commercial landlords: deal pipeline, space availability, tenant and broker activity, portfolio reporting, and the VTS Market and Activate products covering marketing and tenant experience. Its VTS Office Demand Index derives leading indicators from platform activity.
tools.real_estate_use: Office leasing runs on a pipeline that traditionally lived in a leasing director's spreadsheet. VTS makes it institutional: every requirement, tour and proposal is tracked, so an asset manager can forecast occupancy and compare a proposed deal against portfolio standards. Because a large share of US office space transacts on the platform, aggregated tour activity becomes a market signal weeks ahead of signed-lease data.
features: Leasing deal pipeline with tours, proposals and approvals
Space availability and stacking plans
Portfolio occupancy and lease expiry reporting
VTS Market for online marketing of available space
VTS Activate tenant experience application
Office Demand Index from aggregated platform activity

use_cases.job: Forecast occupancy from a real leasing pipeline rather than from a spreadsheet
Track every requirement and proposal on a landlord's portfolio in one system

tools.name: Wattsense
tools.positioning: Plug-in connectivity for buildings too small to justify a full BMS integration project.
tools.description: Wattsense provides a hardware and cloud solution that connects a building's existing equipment — boilers, HVAC, meters, controllers — across multiple protocols and exposes the data and control points through a single cloud API, without a bespoke integration project.
tools.real_estate_use: Most of a commercial portfolio is not headquarters buildings. Mid-sized assets have some automation, no standardisation, and no budget for a systems integrator per site. Wattsense targets exactly that middle: a box on site, protocols handled, data and control available remotely — which is what makes portfolio-wide energy management feasible below the flagship tier.
features: Multi-protocol connectivity to existing building equipment
Cloud API for data collection and remote control
Deployment without a bespoke integration project
Remote monitoring and alerting across sites
Data normalisation across heterogeneous equipment
Partner integrations with energy and facility platforms

use_cases.job: Connect mid-sized buildings to remote monitoring without an integration project each
Standardise data collection across a portfolio of heterogeneous equipment

tools.name: Witco
tools.positioning: The occupant app for French office buildings — services, bookings, access and building communication in one place.
tools.description: Witco provides a white-label mobile application for office buildings and workplaces: room and desk booking, access and badge integration, service requests, on-site retail and concierge services, events, communication and occupant feedback.
tools.real_estate_use: Landlords and corporate occupiers use it as the single interface between the building and the people inside it. Practically, it consolidates what used to be five channels — an email for building notices, a booking tool, a paper ticket for maintenance, a WhatsApp group for events — into one app whose usage data also indicates how the building is really used.
features: White-label occupant mobile app for a building or campus
Room, desk and parking booking
Access control and mobile badge integration
Service requests routed to facilities or providers
Building communication, news and events
Occupant satisfaction measurement and usage analytics

Offer occupants a service layer that supports the rent and the renewal
